prediction.likelyOutcome: Mad Hatter should recover the pre-cutoff back rent (roughly $19,500-$32,000) with high confidence, but its 20-month accelerated rent claim faces a genuine, fact-intensive election-of-remedies and mitigation fight that makes anything close to full acceleration unlikely; Holcomb Dunbar's counterclaim is weak as an affirmative recovery but will meaningfully erode the accelerated-rent number at trial or in settlement.

outcome.description: The trial court granted the landlord summary judgment for all twenty months of unpaid rent (May 2017 through December 2018 at $6,500 a month) plus late fees, $133,900 in total, the full amount claimed in the motion; the tenant's remaining counterclaims went to a jury, which found against it. The Mississippi Court of Appeals affirmed (May 18, 2021) and the Supreme Court of Mississippi, on certiorari, affirmed on March 17, 2022, holding the default letters did not terminate the lease, the election-of-remedies and mitigation arguments were waived, and the alleged breaches were immaterial.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed by the Court of Appeals and, on certiorari, by the Supreme Court of Mississippi.
